text:
Priya Rao: Hi team, trying to install AnyConnect for VPN but installer fails with "Kernel extension blocked" and System Settings shows a pending "Allow system software from developer 'Cisco Systems, Inc.'" prompt that never appears. My Mac says enrolled in Kandji. macOS Ventura 13.5.2, M2.

rachel-it: Welcome! That prompt is a user-approval for kernel extensions (kext) that sometimes gets suppressed by MDM. Two options: (1) We push a Kandji policy to allow Cisco kext by team ID, or (2) grant 30m temp admin so you can click the allow button in Privacy & Security. Which do you prefer?

Priya Rao: Prefer not to be admin if push is quick.

kandji-bot: Kandji action queued: "Allow Cisco KEXT (team ID 9D8F3...)" targeting device Priya-Rao-MBP.

kandji-bot: Kandji policy applied at 2026-03-26T11:05:12Z.

Priya Rao: Rebooted and installer now shows prompt, allowed the extension, AnyConnect install succeeded. VPN connects. Thanks! :raised_hands:

people-ops: Noted for onboarding record.

security-ops: Audit: allowed kext scoped to Cisco bundle/team ID and company images only. If you see unexpected kernel prompts, report immediately.

rachel-it: We'll add this flow to the first-week checklist (kext VPNs often need MDM allowlist). Ping #help if anything else.
